title: SLO debt lane map and cross-team decision log
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a running decision log and a tactical lane map for addressing SLO-related technical debt across product, serving, infra, and platform teams. The goal: create a low-friction way to (1) classify SLO debt, (2) weigh trade-offs against feature work, (3) assign a clear lane owner and recovery policy, and (4) document fallthrough behavior when we cannot meet an SLO during rollouts or capacity events.

Scope:
- Applies to production-facing SLOs for Redwood hosted and dedicated endpoints (latency p95/p99, availability, token-serve success-rate).
- Excludes internal dev-only metrics except where they translate to customer-visible latency/availability.
- Time horizon: Next 90-days tactical plan, with quarterly review.

Context / why this exists:
- We have recurring incidents where model-serving tail latency regresses during bursty workloads (see JIRA-SRE-238).
- Teams often defer reliability work because it competes with revenue-facing features; there is no explicit lane of SLO debt.
- Current rollouts lack a lightweight fallthrough policy for degraded capacity (model fallback, degrade features, traffic shed).

Definitions / quick taxonomy (for triage):
- SLO Debt Category A (Safety-critical): pro-actively owned by SRE + product (examples: auth failures, billing API outages).
- SLO Debt Category B (Customer-impacting): owned by platform + feature team (examples: p99 latency > target for core text generation routes).
- SLO Debt Category C (Efficiency/Cost related): owned by infra/optimize (examples: high token cost due to unbatched requests).

Decision criteria (how we choose what to fix next):
1) Customer impact (severity * exposure)
2) Probability of re-occurrence (historical frequency, traffic patterns)
3) Regression risk for planned rollouts (is a launch scheduled?)
4) Cost to mitigate vs incremental cost of not fixing (include $$$, ops hours, and feature delay)
5) Cross-team coordination overhead (number of teams required)

SLO lane map (who does what):
- Safety-critical lane (A): SRE lead (primary), Product PM (co-owner), Exec escalation. Recovery SLA: 24h hotfix + postmortem 72h.
- Performance lane (B): Platform eng (primary), Serving-runtime eng (support), Feature PM (stakeholder). Recovery SLA: mitigation policy within 48h, prioritized ticket in next sprint.
- Efficiency lane (C): Infra/Optimize (primary), Cost Ops (support). Recovery SLA: 30-day improvement window with benchmarked cost delta.

Fallthrough policies (lightweight rules to apply when SLOs breach during rollouts or capacity constrains):
- If p99 latency > SLO for > 15 minutes and user-facing errors < 0.5%: activate degraded-mode throttling and enable cached-template responses for non-critical routes. Owner: platform oncall.
- If token-serve success-rate < 99% for > 10 minutes: route to smaller model variant (if quality delta acceptable) and alert product-owner for retrospective. Owner: serving-runtime lead.
- If availability below SLO and incident declared: enable global fallback to hosted-API circuit-breaker (limit new sessions) and open war-room. Owner: SRE incident commander.

Decision log (running):
- 2026-01-14: Decision: classify recurring p99 regression on text-gen-v2 as Category B. Rationale: customer-impacting but not safety-critical. Action: platform to schedule a targeted benchmark and ingestion-path audit. Owner: Marco Liu. Linked: JIRA-SRE-238.
- 2026-01-20: Decision: for upcoming webhook rollout, enable automatic routing to quantized model when CPU saturation > 70%. Rationale: prevents large-scale tail latency; quality check acceptable in canary. Action: serving-runtime to implement routing toggle flag. Owner: Jonah Kim.
- 2026-01-28: Decision: adopt a temporary 48h mitigation SLA for Category B items during Q1. Rationale: balance feature momentum and ops backlog. Action: include mitigation SLA in sprint planning. Owner: Priya Desai.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
- How to codify customer-visible degradation messages across SDKs (server-side flag vs client-side UX)? Need UX/product guidance; assigned to Eleni Sarris for a short proposal due 2026-02-12.
- What is the budget threshold where we switch from scale-up to degrade-by-feature? (Finance and product input required). Finance contact: Tom Reynolds (ask: define monthly $ threshold).

Tactical 90-day plan (deliverables and owners):
- Week 1-3: Triage baseline (platform + SRE): add test traffic replay for the top 10 burst patterns, record p95/p99. Owner: Marco Liu. Artifact: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/814
- Week 4-6: Implement lightweight fallthrough toggles (serving-runtime): model routing flag + circuit-breaker hooks. Owner: Jonah Kim.
- Week 7-10: Feature-level degradation playbooks (product + DX): user-facing messaging templates and SDK behavior. Owner: Eleni Sarris.
- Week 11-12: Canary stress and ops drill: simulate capacity events and run the war-room runbook. Owner: Priya Desai / SRE rotation.

Checklist for triage meeting (recurring weekly slot; 30 minutes):
- Bring the latest p95/p99 dashboards for the relevant routes (cost owner: platform).
- Review any SLO breaches in the last 7 days (SRE).
- Confirm lane ownership and outstanding blockers (owners give 1-2 sentence update).
- Decide whether to escalate to IR (incident response) or handle as backlog.
- Update this decision log entry with the chosen mitigation and owner.

Runbook excerpt (for incident commander):
- On SLO breach detection: tag incident as SLO-BREACH and page SRE-PAGE.
- Determine immediate impact (serve success, errors, latency). If errors > 1% escalate to incident.
- If p99 only: enact model fallback policy -> route 20% of traffic to fallback model, monitor quality telemetry for 10 minutes, then increase if stable.
- Post-incident: write a 1-page postmortem; categorize as corrective (code fix), preventative (capacity change), or operational (process tweak).

Metrics to track (dashboard suggestions):
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 latency and request rate (by model variant).
- Token-serve success-rate and error breakdown (auth, infra, model).
- Number of SLO debts open by category and average age.
- Mitigation time (time from breach to mitigation applied).

Communication templates (short):
- Incident stub to customers: "We experienced elevated latency on [route] between [time] and [time]. We applied mitigations and rolled back to normal by [time]. No action required on your end; full postmortem forthcoming."
- Internal exec brief: 2 bullet summary (impact, mitigations, next steps).

Next steps (immediate):
- Action: platform to produce the top-10 burst replay dataset and upload to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-RTY-452). Owner: Marco Liu. Due: 2026-01-20 (in flight).
- Action: serving-runtime to prototype routing toggle in staging. Owner: Jonah Kim. Due: 2026-01-28.
- Action: product/DX to draft degraded-mode UX templates. Owner: Eleni Sarris. Due: 2026-02-12.

Notes / references:
- See JIRA-SRE-238 for incident timeline and initial root-cause hypotheses.
- See github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/814 for replay infra changes.
- This page is intentionally lightweight; if it grows beyond two screens, migrate to a Confluence decision register and link here.

-- End of doc --
